items.title: Count Them If You Got Them
items.summary: Count 'em. Right now. Huh? How much you got? Count. I…
items.content_html:
Count 'em.

Right now.

Huh?

How much you got?

Count.

I don't got cash.

I don't want mean your wallet.

I mean your blessings.

Count them.

Right now.

I hope you got a high number.

But not too high to make you think that's how the world works.

Or maybe I do.

Maybe I do.

I hope it's not low.

Not too low.

Your count has to be above zero blessings.

Zero blessings is broken.

And I'm sorry if you're broken.

You can glue yourself back together, though.

With molten gold.

It's called Kintsugi.

More beautiful, stronger, than ever.

And to those counting high, well, good for you.

Now appreciate 'em.

Big fat kisses for 'em all.

No tongue, though.

Well, maybe for one.

items.title: Call Me Bugs
items.summary: Musings columns are a funny thing. They used to call them…
items.content_html:
Musings columns are a funny thing.

They used to call them blogs but that's just a terrible name.

Blogs.

Yuck.

Not my favorite word.

I tend to write in a way that sometimes contains more meaning than it appears at first glance.

I seek to reward (or at the very least, a muse) the reader for picking up what I'm putting down.

Easter eggs.

Hidden layers.

Buried treasures.

And who doesn't like a treasure hunt?

Not to say all these musings have gems in them.

Some are just turds.

It's part of the fun.

Sifting through all the dirt.

To find the glimmer.

There's a line about glimmer and gold but I don't think it's useful here.

Call me a fool.

🥕

items.title: Over Them Mountains
items.summary: There was a time I could hit a ball a country…
items.content_html:
There was a time I could hit a ball a country mile.

It didn't happen until I was in my 30s.

So that sucks.

But I could.

I could hit a ball into the other fields.

Onto windshields.

Literally rip the hide off 'em.

Now I know I'm starting to sound like Rico Dynamite.

Flinging 🥩s.

My hero.

But what can I say?

I hit bombs.

I haven't picked up a bat in years.

Threw away the one I made in eighth grade not too many years ago.

Still not sure why I did that.

But it was time to put that part of me to rest.

Goodnight.

The thing I learned about hitting (far too late) is you swing down on the ball.

To create lift.

You don't uppercut.

Even though it looks like it.

You generate a back spin on the ball that just crushes it.

Yards it.

Down goes up.

Way up.

Armed with that bit of knowledge, I could still hit 'em out.

But not like I used to.

I'm ok with that.

I'd probably break my coccyx.

⛰

items.title: Infinity / Infinity
items.summary: Cool day today. As far as days go. 8/8. 8.8. I…
items.content_html:
Cool day today.

As far as days go.

8/8.

8.8.

I almost forgot to write.

I suppose I did.

But there's still time.

Thank you for the time.

I don't have much to say.

Except this:

When you sign up for something, do you feel compelled to use all of it to its maximization?

Like you buy a subscription.

And it comes with all sorts of things.

But you only really want the one thing.

Maybe two.

But you feel like by not trying everything, you're somehow "losing" value?

Leaving something on the table.

Perhaps it's just me.

Even if I think the one thing I seek is worth the total price, I still feel like maybe I should try the other stuff since it's basically "free."

And if I don't like the additional stuff, I tend to dislike the subscription in total.

Not worth it.

Yeah, this is pretty much what you get when I almost forget to muse.

I could go on forever forever.

♾♾

items.title: APB
items.summary: For an old(ish) curmudgeon, I'm a happy fellow. Yeah right. No,…
items.content_html:
For an old(ish) curmudgeon, I'm a happy fellow.

Yeah right.

No, I am.

Truly.

Just chipper.

Like if I was in an old movie, I'd be walking with my elbows out, swinging around and circling street lamps.

Helping old ladies across the street.

Tipping my cap to them as I left.

Beaming.

What a kind young oldish man.

Of course, I don't do that.

At least, not anymore.

Ever.

If I did that today, people probably would call a 3-digit number.

I mean, they probably already had the first 2 pre-typed when they saw me.

Elbows out.

Strutting.

Twirling around poles.

Singing.

In the sun.

I don't do rain.

You ain't gonna melt!!!

Yodeling in the golden circle.

...

Be on the lookout for a old(ish) man having a little too much fun. Appears to be singing old show tunes and targeting the elderly.

...

items.title: I Come In Peace
items.summary: As you make your way through this. Through what? Life. Oh.
items.content_html:
As you make your way through this.

Through what?

Life.

Oh.

You attach yourself to certain things.

Like sports teams.

Cliques.

Apparel brands.

Donkeys or elephants.

Flags.

Interests.

Hobbies.

Avocations.

Vocations.

Why?

Most of us do it because it aligns with, or at least represents, a part of us.

It becomes a part of who we are.

There's also some of us who do it because they think it's cool.

Or makes them noticeable.

This is usually folks who, by themselves, would not necessarily be so.

He's talking about luxury watch lovers.

Go Timex!!!

⌚

Nice.

Here's the thing, though.

I'm learning something.

About time.

About time.

I'm learning that this is all meant to divide us.

To keep us busy fighting.

Go Giants!!!

See?

Pay no attention to the man behind the curtain.

As I go up, hopefully I go up, I see that it's all a bit crazy.

I see the world.

And it looks small.

Hello greenish, blue ball.

🌎

With pockets of fights amongst all the pockets of lights.

Everywhere.

Me?

I'm above it all.

Scanning past the pale blue dot.

Looking for aliens.

🛸

Up here.

Starfaring.

💫

Seeing if they wanna rumble.

👽

Or, as Jon B. and Pac used to say, if they're still down.

What you crying for?

items.title: I'll Always Love You Before I Met You
items.summary: I have this annoying habit. Just the one? Where I like…
items.content_html:
I have this annoying habit.

Just the one?

Where I like to sing songs by artists I don't particularly like.

Taylor Dayne, for instance.

Nothing personal, TD.

Just not for me.

But do I like to sing one of her songs now and again.

So I guess it is.

Savage Garden.

🎵 I knew I loved you... 🎶

Not the whole song mind you.

Just the parts that are funny.

The magic is when it gets into my wife's head.

Why am I singing this? Were you singing it earlier?

Why yes.

Yes, I was.

Tee hee.

😊

Whooo whooo hooo hoooh oooh hoooooooh heyyy heyyy heyy.

items.title: Toys R Us Kids
items.summary: One of the interesting things about life is how much I…
items.content_html:
One of the interesting things about life is how much I thought adults had it figured out.

At least, I thought that as a child.

Look at that old dude.

He old.

That man looks like he been through some sheet.

Sweating wisdom.

Instead, many of us old(ish) folk are just kids dressed up in wrinkled clothing.

Hobbies that used to be for kids are now for them all growns up.

And they ready to Venmo.

Video games.

Blocks and figures.

Trading cards.

Traditionally for kids, but now dominated by adults.

They'll fight you (to some degree) in the aisles.

Pretty big industries catering to these kidults.

Yes, that's a term.

And yes, I just learned it.

As a boy, I thought sports cards were fun.

As a man, I reel at the numbers some cards are fetching at auction.

What are we buying here?

A rectangle of cardboard?

Doesn't seem that would be worth much.

Partial ownership of a famous athlete?

That sounds like slavery.

Our youth?

Ouch.

I don't quite understand the allure of it all.

To make money, sure.

But there's something else there.

This market of adults buying stuff that used to be for kids is gigantic.

I don't think a lot of us want to grow up.

And as a former child myself, I understand that part of it.

Not wanting to grow up.

I will leave my conclusion open, because I really don't want to sheet on it.

You do you.

After all.

It's your time.

Spend it how you wish.

Maybe that's the part I wrestle with.

It feels a lot like gambling.

And as an asymmetric bettor myself, you'd think I'd be into that.

But I'm not.

At least I don't think I am.

And that's the part that is interesting.

I used to love GI Joes.

Video games.

Cardboard and inch thick lucite.

But I don't anymore.

I thought I'd have it all action figured out by now.

Pew pew.

items.title: This Is Not Entertaining Advice
items.summary: There's this line. It's kinda hazy. Fuzzy. Opaque. Thick. Now more…
items.content_html:
There's this line.

It's kinda hazy.

Fuzzy.

Opaque.

Thick.

Now more than ever.

And that line separates entertainment from advice.

Entertainment           |||||           Advice

This is not financial advice.

Is what you'll hear.

Then you'd get an hour of financial advice.

Maybe more.

But here's the thing:

Treat what you see online as entertainment.

All of it.

Even, and especially, advice.

The list of people who entertain you can be, and probably should be, limitless.

But the people you heed must be few.

You can, and must, watch folks and just enjoy their schtick.

But for a large part, it's acting.

Playing a part.

Listen to their entertainment.

Don't listen to their advice.

They're aren't giving you it, remember?

This is not legal advice.

A lot of these people, their entire livelihood is centered around talking to a phone.

Or a laptop.

Don't we all do that?

Now like all rules, there are exceptions which prove it.

So exceptionally choose the advice and advicers advisors you follow.

There might be an entertainer out there dropping wisdom, but mostly they are just there to amuse you.

Or infuriate.

Maybe a mix of both.

Please don't take it as gospel.

And for the love of God, don't make any calls that would greatly affect your life based on something or someone you find entertaining.

But I'm just a dude talking through a keyboard.

This musings column is just for entertainment.

My own.

If you like it, sweet.

If not, I get it.

I get it.

Not for everyone.

But remember this last piece of advice:

I'm not giving you any.

items.title: Mind Your Own Beeswax
items.summary: Mind your own business. You ever hear that? It's how I…
items.content_html:
Mind your own business.

You ever hear that?

It's how I grew up.

How I was raised.

Worry about you and yours.

Mouth shut.

And I know that's the city in me.

But it's worked.

For me.

At least I think it has.

People are confounded as to how I can just go on musing about nonsense when the entire world is quite obviously going to sheet.

It is?

But here's the thing.

I don't think it is.

Or at least, at a faster or higher rate than it's always been.

I think we just have access to more people's businesses.

Doomscrolls on the can's worth.

That is a lot.

So we can and often do mind them far more than was ever possible before.

It's a good way to feel wonderful about yourself.

If you're into that.

And a good way to feel bad about yourself.

If you're into that.

Me?

I mind my business.

Someone's got to.

You think these bills pay for themselves?

They don't?

Huh.

🐝🍯🕯
